- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or is weak (negative sentiment → model underreacts).
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts; delay in adjusting forecasts after sentiment changes.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after recent peaks, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Overshoots in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) after strong sentiment upturns; correct by reducing slope or adding downward bias.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model tends to overpredict; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment strength.
- If sentiment is negative and price is trending up, model often fails to recognize reversal; adjust downward by 5–10% of forecasted value.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in upward momentum; reduce forecast slope if sentiment is mixed or declining.
